title: sabline.capabilities/1
description: The capability surface a repository declares its programs may have (sabline-spec SPEC.md section 9): the union of every program's grants and a bound on its fs and net operations, and for each program its own grants, counts and functions' effects. A check derives the same from the working tree and fails when the tree needs more - compared with this document, never with a previous commit. Written and read by sabline-lang from 4.0.0. Within version 1 fields may be added and a consumer must ignore those it does not know, so objects here do not forbid other properties. This schema checks shape. SPEC.md section 9 states what it cannot: that programs are sorted by file, that grants are sorted and reduced (no grant covered by another in the same list), that a port is between 1 and 65535, and how paths are normalised before comparison.

sabline_version.description: Informative: the version of the producer that wrote the document. A checker of another version warns and does not fail for that alone.

date.description: Informative: the day the document was written, UTC.

surface.description: The union of the grants of every program that compiles, reduced, and for fs and net the largest count any of them has.

file.description: The program's path relative to the directory holding the baseline, '/'-separated, with no empty, '.' or '..' component and no backslash.

functions.description: Each function the file defines (not inline function values), mapped to the effects it declares, sorted.

oneOf.description: A program that did not compile: it cannot run, and needs nothing until it does.

counts.description: At most one key per counted effect: a whole number N is at most N operations of that effect in one run (SPEC.md 9.4); null is no bound. A counted effect with grants and no key here has no bound.

grants.description: Grants in the budget grammar of SPEC.md section 4, restricted as section 9.2 says: no counts, one module per ffi: grant, paths as the program writes them, reduced.

anyOf.description: One tool, by name (0.13.0): ASCII letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-', beginning with a letter or '_'. A baseline never holds an argument pattern.
One Python module: text up to the first '.', no ',', '@', ':' or whitespace.
One fs direction under a path, written as the program writes it; no ',' or '@'.
A host name, lower case, optionally with a port; ',' '@' '[' ']' '%' in a name are percent-encoded (SPEC.md 5.2).
A wildcard: '*.' and at least two labels, optionally with a port.
An IPv6 address in brackets, optionally with a port.
